items.title: Father sold car to ease family finances, wins Toyota Vios at Karnival Jom Heboh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A father who had sold his car to ease his family's financial burden ahead of the birth of his second child has struck it lucky, winning a Toyota Vios in a lucky draw at the Jom Heboh Carnival (KJH), held in conjunction with Malaysia Unit Trust Week (MSAM) 2026. I never expected to receive something even better than the car I sold earlier," he said when met at the daily and grand lucky visitor prize presentation ceremony held in conjunction with KJH x MSAM 2026 at Stadium Merdeka. Akhmalluddin said he entered the lucky draw for fun but also took the opportunity to learn about the investment and financial management products offered at MSAM.

items.title: 11 undocumented migrants arrested in Shah Alam raid
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Immigration officers arrested 11 undocumented migrants in a raid on an industrial area in Section U4, Shah Alam. The operation, conducted by the Selangor Immigration Department with Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) and the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters, targeted premises suspected of operating illegally and employing foreign workers without documents. Selangor Immigration Department deputy director (Control) Mohamad Khusairi Kamarudin said all 11 detainees failed to produce travel documents.

items.title: Fire ravages 4 workers' quarters in Kechau
items.summary: KUANTAN: Four workers' quarters at a palm oil mill in Kechau, near Kuala Lipis, caught fire yesterday. In a statement today, Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said two of the semi-permanent terraced houses were completely destroyed, while the other two sustained 80 per cent and 90 per cent damage, respectively. Salahuddin said the department received an emergency call at 3.20pm, and a fire engine from the Kuala Lipis fire station arrived at the scene 18 minutes later.

items.title: Resignation or not, Anwar tells Anthony Loke to show up for transport minister duty
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants Anthony Loke to resume work as transport minister as soon as possible, saying it is hard for him to accept the DAP secretary-general’s proposal to resign. That is why I, as prime minister, find it hard to accept his proposal to resign,” Anwar was quoted as telling reporters at the Youth and Sports Complex in Paroi, Negeri Sembilan where Loke was also present. Loke announced on September 19 that he would resign after the Pardons Board granted former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak house arrest, but he stayed on at Anwar’s request.

items.title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 798, Perak down to 189 this morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak dropped this morning. In SELANGOR, the number of flood victims still housed at relief centres fell to 798 people from 247 families, down from 838 people from 256 families yesterday. In Kuala Selangor, one centre remains open, with 41 evacuees placed at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok In PERAK, the number of evacuees sheltering at three relief centres in three districts dropped slightly to 189 people from 55 families, compared with 197 people from 57 families.

items.title: Walkovers galore for GPS big names, but Dr Sim must fight DAP for Batu Kawah
items.summary: Caretaker Sarawak premier and GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, who retained Gedong, had indicated that GPS had won about 30 seats uncontested, Berita Harian reported today. GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah kept Asajaya for a sixth term after winning without a contest. Also returned unopposed were Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) vice-president Datuk Ibrahim Baki in Satok, Datuk Seri Julaihi Narawi in Sebuyau, Datuk Gerald Rentap Jabu in Layar and Datuk Len Talif Salleh in Kuala Rajang.

items.title: Sarawak polls: GPS wins 29 unopposed, says EC
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has won 29 seats uncontested following the conclusion of the nomination process for the Sarawak election today. The announcement was made by Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. A total of 82 seats are up for grabs in the Sarawak election, which has been fixed for polling on Dec 12.

items.title: Anwar asks Loke to resume duties as transport minister
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has made clear that he wants Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister. Anwar said he found it difficult to accept Loke's intention to step down, despite the Seremban MP having his own reasons for doing so. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Fewer flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak this morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak dropped this morning. In SELANGOR, the number of flood victims still housed at relief centres fell to 798 people from 247 families, down from 838 people from 256 families yesterday. In PERAK, the number of evacuees sheltering at three relief centres in three districts dropped slightly to 189 people from 55 families, compared with 197 people from 57 families.

items.title: Sarawak polls: About 30 GPS seats expected to be won unopposed, says Abang Johari
items.summary: GEDONG, Nov 28 — About 30 seats contested by Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) are expected to be won unopposed following the conclusion of the nomination process for the 13th Sarawak State Election today, said Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. Abang Johari, who is also GPS chairman, said the victories reflected the people’s confidence in the coalition’s leadership and administration in spearheading Sarawak’s development. He said this achievement also showed that the people wanted continuity in the development agenda being implemented by the state government for Sarawak’s future.

items.title: Caterer forgot the extra chicken, and the last students in line got it undercooked at Melaka MRSM
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 28 — A caterer’s oversight left about 100 pieces of chicken short for fasting students at Maktab Rendah Sains MARA (MRSM) Tun Ghafar Baba here, and some students at the back of the queue were served undercooked chicken recently. Melaka state executive councillor Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali said a briefing and visit to the school found that the supplier had failed to factor in extra food for students who were fasting, Berita Harian reported today. Mohd Ridhwan, who is also the Ayer Molek assemblyman, said the school quickly provided alternative food that day and no food poisoning was reported.

items.title: Anwar warns of diabetes risks, calls for healthier lifestyles
items.summary: SEPANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the public to make sports part of their daily lives and watch their diet to build a healthier population. Anwar said Malaysia's high diabetes rate was worrying despite efforts to promote sports and physical activity. "We promote sports and athletics, yet diabetes rates are among the highest.

items.title: Ministry boosts Pedu Dam water storage ahead of expected El Nino
items.summary: KUCHING: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry is increasing water storage at the Pedu Dam in Kedah to ensure sufficient supply for padi field irrigation in the event of an El Nino phenomenon from late next month until April next year. Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the measure was important to ensure padi cultivation, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia, was not affected by water shortages. Mohamad also said adherence to the padi planting schedule was important to avoid water shortages while crops were growing, particularly during a prolonged dry spell.

items.title: Sarawak polls: GPS top leaders among 20 candidates returned unopposed
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has so far won 20 seats uncontested during nomination day for the Sarawak election, reports said. TVS, Suara Sarawak and The Borneo Post reported that those returned unopposed included the two caretaker Sarawak Deputy Premiers, Datuk Douglas Uggah Embas and Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan, in Bukit Saban and Bukit Sari respectively. Others elected unopposed include Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu vice-presidents Datuk Ibrahim Baki (Satok), Datuk Seri Julaihi Narawi (Sebuyau), Datuk Gerald Rentap Jabu (Layar) and Datuk Len Talif Salleh (Kuala Rajang).

items.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas fighters. The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) identified the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, as Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu. World Health Organisation chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus slammed the attack.

items.title: MySiren to undergo simultaneous nationwide test tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Early Warning System (MySiren) will be tested nationwide tomorrow from 10.10am to 10.30am to assess its effectiveness in delivering emergency alerts to mobile phones. Developed using Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology, MySiren simultaneously delivers alerts to compatible mobile devices in affected areas via 4G and 5G networks without consuming mobile data. Authorised disaster management agencies can issue six categories of alerts according to the nature and severity of emergencies, namely National Alert, Extreme Alert, Severe Alert, Missing Person Alert, Test Alert and Exercise Alert.

items.title: Early LRT out of action? Free shuttle buses cover Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum 6.30am–9.30am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Commuters at three Kelana Jaya LRT line stations will wait until 9.30am for their first train tomorrow, instead of the usual 6am start. Rapid KL, the Klang Valley public transport operator, said Kerinchi, Abdullah Hukum and Universiti stations will open late for track replacement work. Free shuttle buses will fill the gap from 6.30am to 9.30am, running every five to 10 minutes between Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi, Abdullah Hukum and Bangsar stations.

items.title: Flash floods catch Manjoi residents in Ipoh off guard
items.summary: IPOH: With floodwaters rising rapidly around her, Nur Aina Aqilah Hanif, 21, was focused on getting three children under her family's care to safety, including an 11-month-old baby. Floodwaters from the overflowing Sungai Tapah surged into their house in Jalan Menteri, Kampung Manjoi, reaching chest level within minutes and trapping the family inside after the strong current damaged the kitchen door. Nur Aina said the ordeal began at about 5pm yesterday, when the water rose so quickly they had little time to react.

items.title: Four-way fight awaits DAP's Kelvin Yii in Batu Lintang
items.summary: KUCHING: DAP's Bandar Kuching member of parliament Dr Kelvin Yii will face a four-cornered fight in his bid to win the Batu Lintang seat in December's Sarawak election. Yii will face Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) See Chee How, Parti Bumi Kenyalang's (PBK) Voon Lee Shan and independent candidate Peter John Jaban. See won the Chinese-majority seat in the last election on a Parti Sarawak Bersatu ticket before later joining GPS component Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP).

items.title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu's Likud of stalling Israeli coalition talks
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, on Friday accused the party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party has in recent days agreed coalition deals with two allied parties, but the route to a parliamentary majority is still far from certain. Eisenkot's Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats party and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party.

items.title: All aboard for Kelantan: State exco, cabbies pin hope on ECRL to bring more visitors
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 28 — Some visitors are expected to take the train to Kelantan for a meal and be back in the Klang Valley by afternoon or night once the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) starts commercial passenger services. Hilmi said hotels, homestays, taxi drivers, eateries and craft sellers stand to benefit, particularly if visitors stay overnight. Md Yusoff said many drivers stopped operating after the Covid-19 pandemic as they could no longer cover living and vehicle maintenance costs.

items.title: China critic in close election race for Taipei mayor
items.summary: TAIPEI: Taiwanese people lined up at polling stations across Taipei on Saturday to cast their ballots in a tight mayoral race, as voting got underway in local elections across the island democracy. China critic Puma Shen is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe seat for the Kuomintang party (KMT), which favours closer ties with Beijing, and become the capital's first Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) mayor in nearly 30 years. Taiwan's local elections are held every four years and will decide races for about 11,000 positions, including mayors and magistrates, across the island democracy's 22 cities and counties.

items.title: Eight killed in Peru military helicopter crash
items.summary: LIMA: A Peruvian air force helicopter carrying military personnel crashed in a coca-growing river basin in the country's southeast, killing eight people and seriously injuring the pilot, the defence ministry said Friday. "Search and rescue operations located the aircraft and the nine military personnel who were on board," the defence ministry said in a statement. Another MI-17 crashed in southern Peru in February killing all 15 on board.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Abang Johari grateful, some 30 GPS candidates set to win uncontested [WATCH]
items.summary: GEDONG: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg described his uncontested victory in the Gedong state seat as a sign of public confidence in the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) administration. He said the victory also reflected the people's trust in the state government's efforts to manage Sarawak's development, particularly through the implementation of the Post-Covid-19 Development Strategy (PCDS) 2030. "Alhamdulillah, it appears that the people of this state want continued development, particularly in Sarawak," he said.

items.title: DAP's Chong Jen, Violet Yong face multi-cornered fights in Kota Sentosa, Pending
items.summary: KUCHING: The only two DAP leaders who won seats in the last Sarawak election will face multi-cornered fights in December's polls. In Kota Sentosa, Sarawak DAP chief Chong Chieng Jen will face Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) Wilfred Yap and Parti Bumi Kenyalang's (PBK) Lue Cheng Hing for the Chinese-majority seat, FMT reported. Meanwhile, Sarawak DAP organising secretary Violet Yong will also face two challengers in her bid to retain Pending.

items.title: Power outage: Police step up security, traffic control in Tawau
items.summary: TAWAU: Police have intensified security and traffic control measures in Tawau amid a power outage affecting Sabah's east coast since Thursday. District police chief assistant commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said maintaining a strong police presence was essential to preventing criminal activities, including cross-border crime and break-ins at commercial and residential premises, particularly at night amid the ongoing power outage. Meanwhile, Rosdi said police were working closely with security agencies and Sabah Electricity to identify areas affected by the power outage, particularly those facing potential security risks.

items.title: Sarawak polls: GPS candidates returned unopposed in Tupong, Bekenu
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secured two more uncontested wins after its candidates were returned unopposed in the Tupong and Bekenu seats, reports said. The Borneo Post reported that GPS candidate Datuk Fazzrudin Abdul Rahman had won the Tupong seat. GPS newcomer Nur Fatin Syafawani Tahamat was also returned unopposed in Bekenu.

items.title: Anwar remembers Chandra Muzaffar as courageous thinker
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembered the late Dr Chandra Muzaffar as a courageous thinker who spoke up for the oppressed and those yearning for justice. "Azizah (Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail) and I extend our condolences to his entire family. Chandra died yesterday at the age of 79.

items.title: Track replacement work will delay services at 3 LRT stations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Track replacement work on the Kelana Jaya LRT line on Sunday will involve Kerinchi, Abdullah Hukum and Universiti stations. Free shuttle buses will operate from 6.30am to 9.30am, connecting Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi, Abdullah Hukum and Bangsar stations. The first phase involved Gombak and Taman Melati stations on Sept 13, 20 and 27, followed by the second phase involving Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations on Nov 15, 22 and 29.

items.title: ECRL expected to boost Kelantan tourist arrivals by 50pct
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Tourist arrivals in Kelantan are expected to increase by up to 50 per cent when the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) begins operations next month. Several sectors, including hotels, homestays, taxi drivers, eateries and handicraft businesses, are expected to benefit from the facility if the visitors are tourists. "We expect ECRL operations to benefit food outlet operators, as many visitors come to Kelantan to enjoy traditional food.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Abang Johari wins Gedong seat unopposed
items.summary: GEDONG: Caretaker Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg has won the Gedong seat unopposed. The Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman secured the seat after his challenger, Sahari Pet, who was expected to contest as an independent candidate, withdrew during the nomination process today. Abang Johari's uncontested victory was announced by returning officer Jamain Wahab about 10.10am today.

items.title: Eight seats in the bag before a single vote: GPS takes Gedong and Tupong
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 28 — Caretaker Sarawak premier and Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg has retained the Gedong state seat without a fight after his was the only nomination accepted today. Returning officer Jamain Wahab announced at 10.06am that Abang Johari had been declared elected uncontested, the news portal said, The Borneo Post reported. Abang Johari first won Gedong in the 12th Sarawak State Election in 2021, after nine terms as Satok assemblyman since 1981, making this his 11th term in the state assembly.

items.title: Sarawak polls: All 82 nomination centres close at 10am
items.summary: KUCHING: All 82 nomination centres for the 13th Sarawak state election closed at 10am today, ending the one-hour nomination period that began at 9am. The focus is also on whether any constituencies will see candidates returned unopposed. The EC has also set Dec 8 for early voting, while polling day is on Dec 12.

items.title: Sarawak polls: 82 nomination centres open simultaneously at 9am
items.summary: Prospective candidates have one hour, until 10am, to submit their nomination papers to the respective returning officers, after which the official list of candidates will be announced. They comprise 82 candidates from Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), 26 from Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS), 14 each from the Democratic Action Party (DAP) and Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK), three from Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) and five independents. Another 13 seats have three candidates , while one seat has four.

items.title: Rain fails to dampen spirits on Sarawak nomination day
items.summary: KUCHING: Early morning rain and overcast skies in several parts of Sarawak, also known as the "Land of the Hornbills", marked the opening of nomination day for the 13th Sarawak state election today, with all 82 state seats up for contest. In Kuching, cloudy skies and drizzle greeted Election Commission (EC) officials, media personnel, prospective candidates and their supporters as they arrived early at various nomination centres, including those for the Kota Sentosa, Tupong and Gedong constituencies. Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), comprising Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), has confirmed that it will contest all 82 seats in a bid to defend the strong mandate it secured in the 12th Sarawak state election.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Annuar Rapaee turns up for Nangka nomination with 1,400 supporters
items.summary: SIBU: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) candidate for the Nangka state seat Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee arrived at the Sarawak Islamic Complex Hall in Sibu at 8.45am. His wife, Datin Dr Haniza Zainal Abidin, accompanied him. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Canada prosecutors seek 25 years for man who sold suicide poison kits
items.summary: NEWMARKET: Canadian prosecutors on Friday requested a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold poison to help people commit suicide, stressing his victims were largely young and experiencing mental distress. Former chef Kenneth Law pleaded guilty earlier this year to aiding 14 suicides in Canada, but he has admitted to selling hundreds of so-called suicide kits globally through a series of online forums. Law's lawyers argued against imposing what could effectively be a life sentence for the 61-year-old.

items.title: Under grey skies, Sarawak’s election race begins as 82 nomination centres open
items.summary: Prospective candidates have one hour, until 10 am, to submit their nomination papers to the respective returning officers, after which the official list of candidates will be announced. They comprise 82 candidates from Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), 26 from Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS), 14 each from the Democratic Action Party (DAP) and Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK), three from Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) and five independent candidates. Another 13 seats have three prospective candidates, while one seat has attracted four.

items.title: Abang Johari seeks to defend Gedong seat
items.summary: GEDONG: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg will face an Independent candidate as he seeks to defend the Gedong state seat in the 13th Sarawak state election. Abang Johari arrived at the Gedong Community Hall nomination centre about 8.40am, accompanied by his proposer, Datuk Seri Mohd Naroden Majais, and seconder Penghulu Francis Kunche. Sahari was accompanied by his proposer, Rambli Jamain, and seconder Jonnie Sahari.

items.title: Zahid hopes exco appointment draws the curtain on Negeri Sembilan crisis
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 28 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes the appointment of six Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (exco) members yesterday will end the political crisis affecting the state. Ahmad Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said Umno and BN express gratitude for the consent of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on the appointment of the exco line-up. The five were Ahmad Zahid, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Parangs, masks and RM20,000 gone: Manjung police on the trail of four men
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 28 — Police are tracking four men, believed to be Indonesian nationals, suspected of involvement in armed gang robberies and attempted housebreakings around Sitiawan and Ayer Tawar near Manjung since Thursday. Manjung police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said police received two reports of gang robberies and four of attempted housebreakings between Thursday and early yesterday. In a separate case, police arrested five locals suspected of involvement in a housebreaking incident in Ipoh on September 11.

items.title: Fadhlina: Putrajaya’s early schooling aid gets parents talking to teachers, not politicians
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 28 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has urged Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi not to equate the distribution of Early Schooling Assistance (BAP) with the Bantuan Kasih Johor (BKJ), as the two initiatives have different contexts and rationales. She said the distribution of BAP, which follows the school calendar, allows parents and teachers to meet face to face, rather than with the prime minister, ministers or any politicians. “This decline needs to be taken seriously,” she said.

items.title: Nomination day for Sarawak kicks off: GPS eyes all 82 seats, DAP going for 14
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 28 — The line-up of candidates contesting the 82 seats in the 13th Sarawak State Election will be known today as nomination takes place across the state. Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, who is defending the Gedong state seat, is scheduled to submit his nomination papers at Dewan Masyarakat Gedong. Several Sarawak federal ministers are also expected to attend nomination centres in their respective parliamentary constituencies to show support for candidates.

items.title: Political scientist Chandra Muzaffar, voice for justice and non-alignment, dies at 79
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Prominent political scientist and International Movement for a Just World (JUST) president Dr Chandra Muzaffar died yesterday at the age of 79. Chandra was well known for his expertise in geopolitics and foreign policy, frequently offering insights into international affairs and advocating Malaysia’s non-aligned approach in navigating global conflicts. An advocate of human rights and social reform, he founded the multi-ethnic reform movement Aliran Kesedaran Negara (Aliran) in 1977 and served as its president until 1991, championing democracy, social justice, good governance and inter-ethnic understanding.

items.title: Confident but still caught: 70pc of Malaysians who meet scammers engage with them, says report
items.summary: It also highlighted that one in seven Malaysian parents (14 per cent) said their children aged seven to 17 had experienced at least one scam. “Scam-recognition confidence in Malaysia skews strongly toward Millennials and Gen X (76 per cent and 78 per cent respectively) and men (75 per cent). “By comparison, a lack of confidence is much higher among those from the Boomer generation (34 per cent), those aged 55+ (25 per cent) and women (20 per cent),” it said.

items.title: RMAF drug smuggling probe: Another air force officer, four civilians held as arrests hit 18
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Another Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer and four civilians were arrested yesterday to assist in investigations into a drug smuggling syndicate that exploited military assets. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the latest arrests brought the total number of suspects detained to 18. He said the arrests followed continued intelligence gathering and questioning of 13 suspects detained earlier in efforts to identify the masterminds behind the drug trafficking activities.

items.title: Grab replaces flat commission model, says drivers deserve pay for pickup distance
items.summary: Grab Malaysia executive director Rashid Shukor said the revised Grab Service Fee (GSF) structure takes pickup time and distance into account when calculating the fee charged to drivers, with the aim of improving their earnings without raising passenger fares. Under the previous arrangement, Grab charged a fixed 30 per cent commission regardless of how far drivers had to travel to collect passengers. Rashid said this had long been a concern among drivers, who argued that they spent time and fuel reaching passengers but still received the same pay.

items.title: Labuan Customs seizes RM18.83m in smuggled goods this year, cars taken off duty-free island top the list
items.summary: LABUAN, Nov 27 — The Labuan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has recorded a total of 167 smuggling-related cases involving seizures, with an estimated value including duties and taxes of RM18.83 million, from Jan 1 to Nov 15 this year. Labuan Customs director Saidin Jalaludin said the department conducted 12 enforcement operations during the period, including five special operations targeting vehicles, cigarettes, alcoholic beverages, drugs and other commodities. “Three vehicle-focused operations, namely Op Radu, Op Radu Bersepadu and Op 90 Plus, resulted in the confiscation of 25 vehicles worth RM4.85 million, including duties and taxes.

items.title: Two ex-Pahang state secretariat staff jailed for slipping names into Datuk award list
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 27 — The Sessions Court here today found two former staff members of the Pahang State Secretary’s Office (SUK) guilty of unauthorised modification of the state’s awards and medals management system website six years ago. Judge Azman Mustapha sentenced Mohd Isa Mohd Yusof, 40, to five years’ imprisonment on 26 charges, while Amer Syafeeq Aziz, 34, received two years’ jail on two charges. The court ordered both accused to serve their sentences concurrently.

items.title: Sandakan facing days of water rationing after power disruptions hit four treatment plants
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Nov 27 — Power supply disruptions and fluctuations have affected operations at four major water treatment plants (WTP) in Sandakan, resulting in water rationing in several areas due to limited production and storage capacity. He said Sabah Electricity Sandakan was working to restore power through local power stations in Libaran, Batu Sapi, Labuk, Seguntor and Mowtas. Walter said the committee would maintain close communication with Sabah Electricity and the Sabah Water Department in Sandakan to monitor restoration efforts and identify assistance needed to minimise the impact on residents.

items.title: Anwar: Masjid Warisan must embody Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Masjid Warisan, to be built in Jalan Davis here, must serve as a symbol of collective pride, blending Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity through architecture that complements modern development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. We want this mosque to be magnificent, but it must also serve a meaningful purpose,” he said when launching the project here today. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: ‘A betrayal of the nation’: Anwar condemns alleged drug smuggling using RMAF aircraft
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the alleged use of a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft for drug smuggling as a serious betrayal of national security, stressing that such actions will not be tolerated. He said border security breaches and the misuse of strategic government assets were among the key issues discussed at today’s Cabinet meeting, following earlier revelations of drug smuggling activities involving commercial flights. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said he had received assurances from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin that strict monitoring and firm action would be implemented immediately.

items.title: Women’s Ministry reviewing child marriage as calls grow for under-18 marriage ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is carrying out two studies related to child marriage in Malaysia, which are expected to be completed early next year. The second study is being conducted through the Malaysian Social Institute (ISM) and is titled “Study on Underage Marriage in Malaysia: Risk Factors, Protective Factors and Prevention Strategies”. While the two studies are being carried out, the ministry said that efforts to address child marriage would continue through the National Child Policy and Action Plan 2026-2030.

items.title: MCMC takes down over 367,000 scam, fake and deepfake posts since 2024
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — A total of 367,537 pieces of harmful content involving online scams, fake accounts, and manipulated imagery, including deepfakes, were removed by service providers following requests from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) between Jan 1, 2024, and Sept 15, 2026. The highest removal rate involved scam-related content, including fake accounts and impersonation, with 303,871 of the 316,215 reported items (96.1 per cent) successfully removed. “Five requests for the removal of content related to financial scams were submitted to licensed service providers under the Online Safety Act 2025 [Act 866], and all such content has been removed,” the ministry stated.

items.title: No deals with US-blacklisted firms, Malaysian companies told after Cabinet briefing on chip curbs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has briefed the Cabinet on United States semiconductor export restrictions, and Malaysian companies have been told not to deal with firms on Washington’s trade blacklist, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. On a separate matter, Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) legal action against Google would not jeopardise the US technology giant’s planned US$15 billion (RM61 billion) investment in Malaysia. Fahmi said regulatory compliance and foreign investment were separate matters, adding that the government’s priority was to ensure Malaysians were protected from harmful online content under the Online Safety Act 2025.

items.title: Ismail Lasim: New exco to take on multiple portfolios as Negeri Sembilan moves to clear state backlog
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Each of the six newly appointed Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members is expected to oversee at least two portfolios to ensure the smooth administration of the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. Ismail said he would ensure that the exco members were assigned related portfolios to make it easier for them to carry out their duties. Ismail said the state government would focus fully on clearing all outstanding papers after exco meetings had not been held for almost two months.

items.title: Not just airports anymore: Cabinet widens anti-narcotics checks to military sites
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Cabinet has agreed to extend anti-narcotics measures at airports to military installations, following the arrests of 13 people, including seven Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, over a drug seizure at the Subang Air Base, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The 17 initiatives between the Home Ministry and Ministry of Transport at strategic locations such as airports have shown to be successful,” Fahmi told reporters at the weekly post-Cabinet press conference here. “But the initiatives do not cover military installations like RMAF airports and so on.

items.title: Johor MB: State reins in data centre water allocations, approves 21 MLD of 73 MLD sought
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor government has approved a total of 21 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water for 19 data centres operating in the state, compared with their initial applications totalling 73 MLD. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the approved allocation represented about 1.05 per cent of Johor’s average treated water production of 2,034MLD. Onn Hafiz, who is also Machap state assemblyman, said that apart from controlling the volume of water allocated, the state government was also encouraging data centres to adopt water-cooling technologies and alternative water sources to reduce their reliance on conventional water supplies.

items.title: DAP adds two more Sarawak seats to stop GPS walking in unopposed
items.summary: Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the decision to contest Bawang Assan and Senadin was made after PKR announced on Nov 24 that it would sit out the polls. He said Lanang MP and Dewan Rakyat Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng would contest Bawang Assan while Sarawak DAP secretary Alan Ling Sie Kiong would contest Senadin. With the two additions, Chong said Sarawak DAP would contest 14 seats in the election.

items.title: Dragon boats race the rain: Penang regatta starts at 8am to beat the storms this weekend
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 27 — The Penang International Dragon Boat Regatta has moved to an 8am start this weekend to beat forecast thunderstorms and fit in more teams, Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said today. He said races will be suspended if heavy rain sets in and resume once it stops, with any races delayed on Saturday moved to Sunday depending on the time lost. — Screengrab from Penang Dragon Boat Facebook page
